tagline.text: The Philippines' leading modern and contemporary art museum, now in BGC

location.label: Location
location.text: MK Tan Centre, 30th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (a good indoor choice in the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,000 (admission to be confirmed, meals included)

children.text: A non-profit art museum that opened in 1976 and is now housed in the MK Tan Centre in BGC. Its permanent and special exhibitions of modern and contemporary Philippine and Southeast Asian art make it a good choice for a rainy day too.

The Metropolitan Museum of Manila (known as "the Met" or "The M") is a non-profit museum centered on modern and contemporary Philippine visual art. According to Wikipedia, it opened on October 3, 1976 inside the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) complex in Malate, Manila, first showing mostly international artists and shifting toward local artists around 1986. In September of that year, seven months after the EDSA Revolution, a new board of trustees was formed and it became a private non-profit rather than a government body. It is run by the Metropolitan Museum of Manila Foundation, Inc., first set up in 1979 by then First Lady Imelda Marcos and businessman Bienvenido Tantoco Sr., and it moved from depending on a BSP subsidy to being foundation-run. Afterward it settled on bilingual exhibition texts and educational programs such as workshops and symposia.

Today the museum is in the MK Tan Centre on 30th Street in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig. Wikipedia says it has had its own premises here since 2022, while one travel blog says it moved from Malate in 2021, so sources differ and the exact opening time cannot be confirmed. The building stands across from Bonifacio High Street and is described as having exhibition space on three floors plus an outdoor area for installations. Supporting companies mentioned include those of the Campos family, NutriAsia and Del Monte Philippines.

The museum's strength is its special exhibitions. One blogger judged that the permanent collection is not large and the real draw is the special shows. As of November 2026, the official site lists, through May 30, 2027, "Miniaturismo to Modernism: Philippine Art from the 19th Century to the Sixties" (curated by Patrick D. Flores) and "Alfonso Ossorio: In My End Is My Beginning." You will enjoy it much more if you check on the official site which exhibitions are on before you go.

BGC is a planned city of shops and restaurants, so it is easy to eat on High Street or stroll in a park after the museum. Its mood is completely different from the historic districts of central Manila, which makes it a fitting half-day for seeing one side of modern Manila. The BGC High Street and Track 30th Park are within walking distance of the museum, so it is easy to continue with a meal or a walk after your visit. It suits travelers who want to add one more well-known museum, who look for an indoor plan on a rainy day, or who are interested in contemporary Philippine art.

This exhibition, put together by curator Patrick D. Flores, is held in the North and South Galleries on the third floor. It follows the course of Philippine art from 19th-century artists such as Damian Domingo and Juan Luna to the modernist period of the 1960s and David Medalla. The official site lists the period from November 8, 2026 to May 30, 2027.
This show, in the North Gallery on the second floor, introduces the work of the Philippine-born American artist Alfonso Ossorio from the 1930s to the 1990s. It runs during the same period.

blocks.title: A collection centered on modern and contemporary art

children.text: Modern and contemporary Philippine art is the heart of the collection, and a 2026 news report says it also includes Southeast Asian works from the Del Monte Collection. There is an assessment that the permanent display is not large, so it is best seen together with a special exhibition.

The exhibition space on three floors inside the MK Tan Centre is known to have been designed by architect Carlos Arnaiz (CAZA). There is also an outdoor installation area. The ticket office and one gallery are on the right as you enter at ground level, and you take the elevator to the rest.

There are records that in its earlier Malate years, the museum showed ancient goldwork and pottery from the 8th to 13th centuries, religious art and works by Félix Hidalgo as a permanent display inside the BSP complex. It is not confirmed whether those works are still on view in BGC, so check the official information.
The official site says that a printmaking series workshop, open to anyone aged 12 and up, is held on Saturdays from mid-2026 through November. Check the Instagram announcements for exact dates.
The official site says that a ticket includes all galleries, the museum shop and special exhibitions. After the exhibits you can look around the shop for souvenirs and catalogs.

"Banksy Universe," held from May 14 to November 20, 2024, drew attention when the museum said the show was "not authorized or endorsed" by Banksy. Banksy's agency denied any involvement, and there was also criticism over street-art restrictions in BGC and the commercial setting.

children.text: Enter at the weekend opening time (

Start with the Alfonso Ossorio exhibition in the second-floor North Gallery. Follow his work in order from the 1930s to the 1990s.

Programs such as printmaking workshops may be held on Saturdays, so check the official Instagram announcements.

items.title: By taxi or Grab from Manila or Makati

children.text: Take a Grab or taxi from Makati or central Manila and set the destination as "MK Tan Centre, 30th Street, BGC." The BGC entrances get congested during rush hours, so allow extra time.
From High Street, it is across from TGI Fridays; from Lane P, it is across from Track 30th Park.
There are bus routes into BGC from Manila and Makati as well as BGC circulator buses, but routes and operating hours change often. Check the latest information locally.
Inside BGC it is easy to get around on foot.
You can park at Two Parkade right next to the museum, and there is additional paid parking nearby.
The official site says buses need a parking permit from BGC, and vans can park at the museum building.
It is an indoor museum, so the season hardly affects it. If anything, it works well as an indoor plan in the hot, humid months of March–May or the rainy season from June to October.
Hours are Tuesday–Friday
and Saturday–Sunday
; the museum is closed on Mondays. Weekends can be busier, so weekday afternoons are more relaxed.

BGC, where the museum is located, has restaurants and cafés clustered along High Street and in nearby malls, which makes meals before or after your visit convenient. For specific places, consult recent reviews in a local map app. Assuming the visit takes about two hours, it is easy to plan either a museum visit followed by lunch, or lunch followed by the museum and a café break.

BGC has many large hotels and serviced apartments and is close to Makati. Staying in BGC and making the museum one part of a BGC itinerary is also convenient. Room rates vary greatly by season and date, so check on a booking site.
Before you go, check the current special exhibitions on the official site (metmuseum.ph). Some reviewers say the permanent displays alone can feel thin.
The other galleries beyond the ground-floor one are reached through the building's shared hallway and by elevator, so follow the signs carefully.
The museum is closed on Mondays, and the last entry is
Tickets bought through the online booking page are said to be final and non-refundable. Book when your plans are certain.
Discounts for students, seniors and PWD require valid verification, so bring your ID.
Combining the museum with a meal on BGC High Street makes an efficient half-day.
The official site does not state photography or bag rules, so check at the entrance.
Make sure you go to the current address in BGC and not the old BSP complex location in Malate.
Old sources and some blogs list the BSP complex in Malate (Roxas Boulevard) as the address. The museum is now at the MK Tan Centre in BGC. Check the official site before you go.
Admission prices and free days differ between sources, so confirm them on the official site's booking page. Figures such as ₱100 in older sources come from the Malate years.
Exhibitions run for set periods, so you may not be able to see the same works again.
During rush hours the roads to BGC are very congested, so use public transport or travel earlier.
During special exhibitions the museum can get crowded. Go early in the morning on weekends.
There may be temporary closures for typhoons or events, so check official announcements.
The planned city where the museum is located, with restaurants and shops on High Street, parks and street art.
A financial and commercial hub close to BGC with many malls and restaurants. It is easy to continue there after the museum.
The National Museum in central Manila covers classical Philippine art and natural history broadly. If you want to follow modern and contemporary art with classical art, add it to your itinerary.
A cultural complex along Roxas Boulevard by Manila Bay that hosts performances and exhibitions. In the old Malate years, the museum was on the same Roxas Boulevard route.
